front: Longtemps, je me suis couché de bonne heure.
pronunciation: [lohn-TAHN, zhuh muh swee koo-shay duh bun UHR]
back: For a long time, I went to bed early.
context: The famous first line of Proust's 'À la recherche du temps perdu' (1913).

front: Le goût de la madeleine fait resurgir toute son enfance.
pronunciation: [luh goo duh lah mad-LEN feh ruh-sür-zheer toot sohn nahn-FAHNS]
back: The taste of the madeleine brings back his whole childhood.
context: 'La madeleine de Proust' = any sensation that triggers a vivid memory.

front: Aujourd'hui, maman est morte.
pronunciation: [oh-zhoor-DWEE, mah-mahn eh MORT]
back: Mother died today.
context: Opening of Camus's 'L'Étranger' (1942). Its flat tone is the whole novel.

front: Il faut imaginer Sisyphe heureux.
pronunciation: [eel foh ee-mah-zhee-nay see-ZEEF uh-RUH]
back: One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
context: Last line of Camus's 'Le Mythe de Sisyphe': the philosophy of the absurd.

front: Il faut cultiver notre jardin.
pronunciation: [eel foh kül-tee-vay noh-truh zhar-DAN]
back: We must cultivate our garden.
context: The conclusion of Voltaire's 'Candide' (1759): focus on useful work rather than idle theory.

front: Demain, dès l'aube, à l'heure où blanchit la campagne, je partirai.
pronunciation: [duh-MAN, deh LOHB, ah luhr oo blahn-shee lah kahm-PAN-yuh, zhuh par-tee-REH]
back: Tomorrow, at dawn, when the countryside turns white, I will set out.
context: Victor Hugo's poem to his daughter Léopoldine, who drowned in 1843. Learned by heart in school.

front: Jean Valjean est le héros des Misérables.
pronunciation: [zhahn val-ZHAHN eh luh ay-ROH day mee-zay-RAH-bluh]
back: Jean Valjean is the hero of Les Misérables.
context: Hugo's 1862 novel. Note: 'le héros' has an aspirated h, so no liaison.

front: Là, tout n'est qu'ordre et beauté, luxe, calme et volupté.
pronunciation: [LAH, too neh kor-dray boh-TAY, lüks, kalm ay voh-lüp-TAY]
back: There, all is order and beauty, luxury, calm and pleasure.
context: Refrain of Baudelaire's 'L'Invitation au voyage', from 'Les Fleurs du mal' (1857).

front: Les Fleurs du mal ont fait l'objet d'un procès pour outrage aux bonnes mœurs.
pronunciation: [lay fluhr dü MAL ohn feh lob-zheh dan proh-SEH poor oo-trahzh oh bun MUHRS]
back: Les Fleurs du mal was prosecuted for offending public morals.
context: Six poems were banned until 1949. Flaubert faced a similar trial for 'Madame Bovary'.

front: Je est un autre.
pronunciation: [zhuh eh tan NOH-truh]
back: I is someone else.
context: Rimbaud (1871). The deliberate grammar 'je est' expresses a split self.

front: Ô temps ! suspends ton vol.
pronunciation: [oh TAHN ! süs-pahn tohn VOL]
back: O time, suspend your flight!
context: Lamartine, 'Le Lac' (1820): the Romantic plea to stop time.

front: Rodrigue, as-tu du cœur ?
pronunciation: [roh-DREEG, ah-tü dü KUHR]
back: Rodrigue, have you courage?
context: Corneille, 'Le Cid' (1637). 'Le cœur' here means courage. 'Un dilemme cornélien' = a choice between love and duty.

front: La langue de Molière est réputée difficile.
pronunciation: [lah lahng duh moh-LYEHR eh ray-pü-tay dee-fee-SEEL]
back: French is reputed to be difficult.
context: 'La langue de Molière' = French, as English is 'the language of Shakespeare'.

front: On ne voit bien qu'avec le cœur. L'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux.
pronunciation: [ohn nuh vwah byan kah-vek luh KUHR. leh-sahn-SYEL eh tan-vee-zee-bluh poor lay ZYUH]
back: One sees clearly only with the heart. What is essential is invisible to the eye.
context: The fox's secret in Saint-Exupéry's 'Le Petit Prince' (1943), the most translated French book.

front: Ce roman est un chef-d'œuvre du réalisme.
pronunciation: [suh roh-MAHN eh tan sheh-DUH-vruh dü ray-ah-LEESM]
back: This novel is a masterpiece of realism.
context: 'Chef-d'œuvre' (plural 'chefs-d'œuvre'). Realism: Balzac, Flaubert, Maupassant.

front: Zola est le chef de file du naturalisme.
pronunciation: [zoh-LAH eh luh shef duh feel dü nah-tü-rah-LEESM]
back: Zola is the leading figure of naturalism.
context: 'Le chef de file' = the leader of a movement.

front: J'accuse… !
pronunciation: [zhah-KÜZ]
back: I accuse…!
context: Zola's 1898 open letter defending Dreyfus. Now used for any public denunciation.

front: L'intrigue se déroule dans le Paris du XIXe siècle.
pronunciation: [lan-TREEG suh day-rool dahn luh pah-REE dü deez-nuh-vyem SYEH-kluh]
back: The plot takes place in 19th-century Paris.
context: 'L'intrigue' = the plot. 'Se dérouler' = to take place.

front: Le narrateur reste anonyme tout au long du récit.
pronunciation: [luh nah-rah-TUHR rest ah-noh-NEEM too toh lohn dü ray-SEE]
back: The narrator remains anonymous throughout the story.
context: 'Le récit' = the narrative.

front: Le dénouement est inattendu.
pronunciation: [luh day-noo-MAHN eh tee-nah-tahn-DÜ]
back: The ending is unexpected.
context: 'Le dénouement' = the resolution of the plot (literally 'untying').

front: C'est un recueil de nouvelles de Maupassant.
pronunciation: [seh tan ruh-KUHY duh noo-VEL duh moh-pah-SAHN]
back: It's a collection of short stories by Maupassant.
context: 'Un recueil' = a collection. 'Une nouvelle' = a short story (and a piece of news).

front: L'alexandrin compte douze syllabes.
pronunciation: [lah-lek-sahn-DRAN kohnt dooz see-LAB]
back: The alexandrine has twelve syllables.
context: The classic French verse line, used by Racine and Corneille.

front: Il faut prononcer le e muet pour respecter la métrique.
pronunciation: [eel foh proh-nohn-say luh uh mü-EH poor res-pek-tay lah may-TREEK]
back: You have to pronounce the silent e to respect the meter.
context: In poetry, the 'e muet' often counts as a syllable before a consonant.

front: Cette pièce de Racine est une tragédie classique.
pronunciation: [set pyes duh rah-SEEN eh tün trah-zhay-DEE klah-SEEK]
back: This play by Racine is a classical tragedy.
context: The classical rule of the three unities: time, place and action.

front: La mise en scène est audacieuse.
pronunciation: [lah mee zahn SEN eh toh-dah-SYUHZ]
back: The staging is bold.
context: 'La mise en scène' = direction (theater or film).

front: C'est une œuvre engagée.
pronunciation: [seh tün NUH-vruh ahn-gah-ZHAY]
back: It's a politically committed work.
context: 'La littérature engagée' was championed by Sartre after the war.

front: Simone de Beauvoir a écrit Le Deuxième Sexe en 1949.
pronunciation: [see-mun duh boh-VWAHR ah ay-kree luh duh-zyem SEKS ahn mee-nuhf-sahn-kah-rahnt-NUHF]
back: Simone de Beauvoir wrote The Second Sex in 1949.
context: A founding text of modern feminism.

front: Marguerite Yourcenar fut la première femme élue à l'Académie française.
pronunciation: [mar-guh-reet yoor-suh-NAR fü lah pruh-myehr fam ay-lü ah lah-kah-day-mee frahn-SEZ]
back: Marguerite Yourcenar was the first woman elected to the Académie française.
context: In 1980. Note the passé simple 'fut', typical of written biography.

front: Annie Ernaux a reçu le prix Nobel de littérature en 2022.
pronunciation: [ah-nee ehr-NOH ah ruh-sü luh pree noh-BEL duh lee-tay-rah-TÜR ahn duh-meel-van-DUH]
back: Annie Ernaux received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2022.
context: Known for autobiographical writing about class and memory.

front: Le prix Goncourt est le prix littéraire le plus prestigieux.
pronunciation: [luh pree gohn-KOOR eh luh pree lee-tay-REHR luh plü pres-tee-ZHYUH]
back: The Goncourt is the most prestigious literary prize.
context: Awarded each November. The prize money is just 10 euros, but sales soar.

front: La rentrée littéraire voit paraître des centaines de romans.
pronunciation: [lah rahn-tray lee-tay-REHR vwah pah-reh-truh day sahn-ten duh roh-MAHN]
back: The literary season sees hundreds of novels published.
context: Every late August to October, French publishers release their big titles.

front: La critique est unanime : c'est un chef-d'œuvre.
pronunciation: [lah kree-TEEK eh tü-nah-NEEM : seh tan sheh-DUH-vruh]
back: The critics are unanimous: it's a masterpiece.
context: 'La critique' = critics collectively; 'une critique' = a review.

front: Ce film a reçu des critiques élogieuses.
pronunciation: [suh feelm ah ruh-sü day kree-teek zay-loh-ZHYUHZ]
back: This film received rave reviews.
context: 'Élogieux' = full of praise. Opposite: 'des critiques assassines'.

front: Franchement, ce film est un navet.
pronunciation: [frahnsh-MAHN, suh feelm eh tan nah-VEH]
back: Frankly, this film is a turkey.
context: 'Un navet' (a turnip) = a terrible film or book.

front: La Nouvelle Vague a révolutionné le cinéma à la fin des années 50.
pronunciation: [lah noo-vel VAHG ah ray-voh-lü-syoh-nay luh see-nay-MAH ah lah fan day zah-nay san-KAHNT]
back: The New Wave revolutionized cinema in the late 1950s.
context: Godard, Truffaut, Varda, Chabrol: handheld cameras, real streets, jump cuts.

front: Les Quatre Cents Coups est le premier long métrage de Truffaut.
pronunciation: [lay kat-ruh sahn KOO eh luh pruh-myay lohn may-TRAHZH duh trü-FOH]
back: The 400 Blows is Truffaut's first feature film.
context: 'Faire les quatre cents coups' = to run wild. 'Un long métrage' = a feature film.

front: À bout de souffle a imposé le style de Godard.
pronunciation: [ah boo duh SOO-fluh ah an-poh-ZAY luh steel duh goh-DAR]
back: Breathless established Godard's style.
context: 'À bout de souffle' (1960) = out of breath.

front: La Palme d'or est décernée au Festival de Cannes.
pronunciation: [lah palm DOR eh day-sehr-nay oh fes-tee-val duh KAN]
back: The Palme d'Or is awarded at the Cannes Film Festival.
context: 'Décerner' = to award (a prize).

front: Ce film est en version originale sous-titrée.
pronunciation: [suh feelm eh tahn vehr-syohn oh-ree-zhee-NAL soo-tee-TRAY]
back: This film is in the original language with subtitles.
context: 'VOST' on cinema listings; 'VF' = dubbed into French.

front: Les impressionnistes peignaient en plein air.
pronunciation: [lay zan-preh-syoh-NEEST peh-nyeh tahn plan NEHR]
back: The Impressionists painted outdoors.
context: The name came from Monet's 'Impression, soleil levant' (1872), mocked by a critic.

front: Le musée d'Orsay abrite la plus grande collection impressionniste au monde.
pronunciation: [luh mü-zay dor-SAY ah-breet lah plü grahnd koh-lek-SYOHN an-preh-syoh-NEEST oh MOHND]
back: The Musée d'Orsay houses the world's largest Impressionist collection.
context: A former railway station on the Left Bank.

front: Je suis invité au vernissage de l'exposition.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zan-vee-tay oh vehr-nee-SAHZH duh lek-spoh-zee-SYOHN]
back: I'm invited to the opening of the exhibition.
context: 'Le vernissage' = the private view (originally the varnishing of paintings).

front: Ce tableau est une nature morte.
pronunciation: [suh tah-BLOH eh tün nah-tür MORT]
back: This painting is a still life.
context: 'Une nature morte' = still life; 'un autoportrait' = a self-portrait.

front: La palette du peintre est très lumineuse.
pronunciation: [lah pah-let dü PAN-truh eh treh lü-mee-NUHZ]
back: The painter's palette is very luminous.
context: 'La palette' = the range of colors used.

front: Le style de cet auteur est dépouillé.
pronunciation: [luh steel duh set oh-TUHR eh day-poo-YAY]
back: This author's style is spare.
context: 'Dépouillé' = stripped down. Opposite: 'ampoulé' (bombastic).

front: Ce roman m'a profondément bouleversé.
pronunciation: [suh roh-MAHN mah proh-fohn-day-mahn bool-vehr-SAY]
back: This novel deeply moved me.
context: 'Bouleverser' = to move deeply, overwhelm.

front: L'œuvre se prête à plusieurs lectures.
pronunciation: [LUH-vruh suh pret ah plü-zyuhr lek-TÜR]
back: The work lends itself to several interpretations.
context: 'Une lecture' = a reading, interpretation.

front: Le personnage principal incarne la révolte de toute une génération.
pronunciation: [luh pehr-soh-nahzh pran-see-PAL an-karn lah ray-VOLT duh toot ün zhay-nay-rah-SYOHN]
back: The main character embodies the revolt of a whole generation.
context: 'Incarner' = to embody.

front: Madame Bovary, c'est moi.
pronunciation: [mah-dam boh-vah-REE, seh MWAH]
back: Madame Bovary is me.
context: Attributed to Flaubert, though there's no written proof he said it.

front: Mignonne, allons voir si la rose…
pronunciation: [mee-NYUN, ah-lohn vwahr see lah ROHZ]
back: Sweetheart, let us go and see whether the rose…
context: Ronsard (1545): the Renaissance 'carpe diem' poem about fleeting youth.
